title: Gaming since I was 6, no art or music skills: in 2 months, AI tools let me build a free demo of my childhood dream game, solo
author: Daikooku
selftext:
Hi! I've mentioned this project in a few comments here, and the free demo of **KAGEKARI** is now out: a top-down survivors-like roguelite in feudal Japan where you hunt yokai as a shinobi.

A bit about me: I'm 35, a dad of two, and I've been gaming since I was 6 (Zelda, Diablo, Final Fantasy, Pokémon, WoW). Making a game was my childhood dream, and AI tools are what finally made it possible for me to do it alone.

**Some numbers:** about 2 months of work, \~320 hours of sessions with AI, 530 commits, 2 regions of 12 waves, bosses and mini-bosses + 2 secret bosses, Japanese voice acting with EN/FR subtitles, 1 to 3 hours to finish the demo.

**How each part was made:**

* **Code (Unity 6, C#):** written with Claude Code under my direction. I also use Codex as a second reviewer: it audits whole areas (saves, controller, balancing) and Claude fixes what it finds.
* **Sprites and effects:** PixelLab.
* **Illustrations** (ink-wash codex, ema plaques, prologue, cover art): Gemini.
* **Music:** ACE-Step. **Sound effects:** Stable Audio Open + some synthesized in Python.
* **Voices:** Japanese and French lines with Qwen3-TTS (voice design) and Chatterbox (cloning a reference voice so each character keeps the same timbre).

**What I learned:**

* The AI writes, but **I decide**: the design, the yokai, the balancing and every choice are mine. Most of my time goes into testing, choosing between versions and asking for changes.
* **Playtest logs are gold.** The game writes a JSON journal of every run (damage taken by source, choices, deaths). A friend's 16 runs showed one enemy caused 8 of his 11 deaths, so we toned it down.
* Generating voices that stay consistent was the hardest part: a designed voice changes timbre between takes; cloning a single reference fixed it.

What I'd love to know most: is it fun? Am I on the right track? Happy to answer questions about the workflow too.

[https://daiko-kobo.itch.io/kagekari](https://daiko-kobo.itch.io/kagekari)

comments.author: alhanyk
comments.body:
You only get a few seconds to grab a player. 

I hit the big Start button and the game launched in my mobile browser, but didn't actually work. The "device not supported" note is in small print, and nobody reads that before tapping Start. 

Most people won't give it a second try. I'd block mobile with a clear message on the button itself, or make it work there.

replies.author: Daikooku
replies.body: You’re totally right, thanks for taking the time to say it. KAGEKARI is keyboard/controller only for now, and that small note wasn’t enough. I just added a proper mobile screen: on a phone it now tells you right away to play on PC instead of loading a broken game. If you get a chance to try it on a computer, I’d love to hear what you think!
